purpose: Sourced requirements table + costed spec-compliant retry spec for leg 353's DSSP-NKBASIN NO (route 4 stop). Not a re-adjudication of leg 353's verdict.

predecessor.verdict: NO: matrix-free Newton (plain line search) recovered 0/5 published RPOs from Lucas & Kerswell 2015 Table IV, DNS T_total=2000
declared_simplifications: DNS length: T_total=2000 (this leg's affordable window)
globalization: plain-Newton line search, not hookstep/trust-region
predecessor.target_class: RPOs (nonzero x-shift s, e.g. UPO37 s=0.375) -- NOT plain periodic orbits (s=m=0)

sourced_requirements_table.role: the paper whose Table IV RPOs leg 353 tried to recover
sourced_requirements_table.dns_length_T: 5e6 ("an extended DNS was conducted to T=5x10^6 which is 50 times longer than each of the 3 runs analysed in [Chandler & Kerswell 2013]")
sourced_requirements_table.attempted_window: R<0.25 AND 0.5<T<60 (5120 of 11934 total near-recurrence guesses actually fed to Newton; rest skipped as out of useful range)
sourced_requirements_table.globalization_method: Newton-GMRES-hookstep (same algorithm as Chandler & Kerswell 2013), GPU-accelerated time-stepping
sourced_requirements_table.reported_success_rate: ~10% at R>=0.2 (their own words: "the chances of converging a guess settle to about 10% for R >~ 0.2", Fig. 3) -- leg 353's 5 attempts sat at R=0.177-0.263, i.e. squarely in this ~10%-success regime per the source paper itself
sourced_requirements_table.net_yield: 81 unique converged recurrent flows from 5120 attempted guesses (raw per-guess convergence rate is higher than this net figure because of heavy duplication into the same few dozen distinct solutions)
sourced_requirements_table.quote_pinning_note: leg 353's 0/5 result is NOT anomalous relative to this source's own reported success curve at matching residual

sourced_requirements_table.role: origin of the Re=60 2D Kolmogorov recurrent-flow search + the Newton-GMRES-hookstep implementation both 1406.1820 and leg 353 descend from
sourced_requirements_table.dns_length_T: 1e5 per run (3 runs at Re=60: e,f,g); Series B (nonzero-shift RPO search) at Re=60 used 3e5 (run p)
sourced_requirements_table.recording_threshold_Rthres: 0.3 at Re=60 (0.15 too restrictive at Re=40, relaxed; 0.35/0.4 needed at Re=80/100)
sourced_requirements_table.globalization_method: Newton-GMRES-Hookstep, max Newton=75, max GMRES=500, max Hookstep=50 iterations ("fairly conservative limits" per the authors)

reported_success_rate.Re60_seriesB_nonzero_shift_true_RPOs: 7/163 (4.3%) -- run p, THE CLASS UPO37 BELONGS TO (s=0.375 != 0)

sourced_requirements_table.wall_clock_reported: "typically lead to run times of a couple of months for each of the Re=60, 80 and 100 runs" on a single Xeon X5670 CPU core (pre-GPU); Re=40 had to be subdivided 12 ways to be manageable
sourced_requirements_table.quote_pinning_note: the RPO-specific success rate (4.3%) is an order of magnitude below the plain-periodic-orbit rate (62-74%) at the SAME DNS length and SAME hookstep code -- UPO37 is in the harder class even in the source's own hands

sourced_requirements_table.paper: Viswanath 2007, J. Fluid Mech. 580, 339 ("Recurrent motions within plane Couette turbulence")
sourced_requirements_table.role: origin of the hookstep methodology itself, cited by both Kolmogorov-flow papers above as the source of their algorithm
sourced_requirements_table.dns_length_T: not the paper's focus (plane Couette flow, different system); not extracted as a comparable number
sourced_requirements_table.recurrence_threshold: not applicable in the same form (different recurrence-detection scheme for that system)
sourced_requirements_table.globalization_method: locally-constrained optimal hookstep in a Krylov (GMRES/Arnoldi) subspace -- SVD-based trust-region step on the Hessenberg system, radius adapted step-to-step by comparing actual vs. predicted error reduction (Dennis & Schnabel 1996 trust-region machinery)
sourced_requirements_table.load_bearing_quote: "the Newton step by itself never leads to convergence. The widely used expedient of damping the Newton step is also ineffective."
sourced_requirements_table.significance: SOURCED, DIRECT confirmation that leg 353's globalization gap (plain-Newton line search = a form of step damping) is the ALGORITHM CLASS the hookstep literature explicitly built itself to replace, not merely a slower version of the same approach -- the founding paper of this methodology states in so many words that leg 353's approach is expected not to work on this problem class, independent of DNS length

refusals_to_measure.observed: HTTP 429 "Rate exceeded" on every attempt across ~5 retries with 15-30s backoff, spanning several minutes
refusals_to_measure.diagnosis: shared IP-based rate limit, plausibly contended by the 4-leg-parallel roster hitting the same export API concurrently (leg 326 banked a similar 429 pattern on a different day)
refusals_to_measure.banked_as: REFUSAL, not silently dropped -- worked around by fetching PDFs directly from arxiv.org/pdf/<id> (HTTP 200 every time, no rate limiting observed on that path), which is how all four sourced papers were actually retrieved
refusals_to_measure.environment_fact: arxiv.org direct PDF fetch and WebFetch of arxiv.org/abs pages both work reliably from this container; only the export.arxiv.org search/query API is rate-limited under concurrent leg load

refusals_to_measure.banked_as: REFUSAL for the listing-page route; worked around by fetching the known arXiv ID (physics/0604062) directly by title-recall + direct PDF URL guess, which succeeded (HTTP 200) -- the paper was NOT located via arXiv search, it was located by domain knowledge of the citation and confirmed by successful fetch + content match (hookstep, Newton-GMRES, trust region, plane Couette all present in the fetched text)

costed_retry_spec.what_spec_compliance_means_here: matching leg 353's own two DECLARED simplifications (DNS length, globalization) at whatever level the sourced literature actually used -- NOT necessarily matching resolution (leg 353 used N=24; the literature's 'full' recurrence check used a much finer grid, Nx=Ny=128 per 1406.1820's own text on its reduced-criterion speedup -- resolution was never one of leg 353's declared gaps, so it is flagged separately below, not folded into this cost)

requirement_1_globalization.what: implement a genuine locally-constrained optimal hookstep (Viswanath 2007 sec 2.3 / Dennis-Schnabel trust region) inside the existing matrix-free GMRES Newton loop, replacing the plain line search
requirement_1_globalization.cost_estimate: 1 leg, standard difficulty -- this is a self-contained numerical-methods implementation task (SVD on a small Hessenberg system, ~d<30 per Viswanath's own note) that can be unit-tested and validated against leg 353's own control case (the 1%-perturbed laminar fixed point, which line-search-Newton already converges cleanly on) before being pointed at the hard RPO targets
requirement_1_globalization.compute_cost: negligible (unit tests + control-case validation, seconds-to-minutes, no long DNS needed for this leg)

requirement_2_dns_length.what: extend the recurrence-search DNS from T=2000 to a spec-compliant window
requirement_2_dns_length.minimum_spec_compliant: T=1e5 (Chandler & Kerswell's per-run length at Re=60, the SHORTEST of the three sourced DNS lengths, and the one that first produced UPO37's neighbors)
requirement_2_dns_length.full_literature_scale: T=5e6 (Lucas & Kerswell's extended run, 50x the above)

compute_cost_same_resolution_N24.measured_rate: 352.3256s wall for T_total=2000 (200000 steps at dt=0.01) => 1.7616 ms/step
compute_cost_same_resolution_N24.caveat: linear extrapolation of leg 353's own measured, pure-numpy CPU pseudospectral rate; no GPU path exists in this leg's solver stack, unlike the literature (1406.1820 explicitly used GPU-accelerated time-stepping to make T=5e6 tractable, and 1207.4682's pre-GPU Re=60/80/100 runs each took 'a couple of months' on a single CPU core at their own resolution)

requirement_3_attempt_count.what: run enough independent Newton attempts to be a meaningful test against the literature's OWN reported RPO success rate, not just re-run the same 5
requirement_3_attempt_count.sourced_baseline: Chandler & Kerswell's Re=60 nonzero-shift (RPO) success rate is 4.3% (7/163); Lucas & Kerswell's own success rate at R>=0.2 (leg 353's exact residual regime) is ~10%
requirement_3_attempt_count.implication: at a true 4-10% per-attempt success rate, 5 attempts have an ~59-77% chance of zero successes EVEN IF THE SOLVER AND DNS WERE FULLY SPEC-COMPLIANT -- leg 353's 0/5 is statistically uninformative at this sample size regardless of which of the two declared gaps is fixed first
requirement_3_attempt_count.minimum_n_for_a_meaningful_test: ~50-100 independent Newton attempts (matching the order of magnitude of guesses the source papers themselves fed their hookstep code per Re before declaring a recurrent-flow catalogue)

compute_cost.per_attempt_hookstep_scaled_estimate: 3-5x leg 353's per-attempt cost at the source's own max_newton=75/max_gmres=500 limits (more iterations allowed before giving up) => ~600-1000s/attempt

minimum_viable_spec_compliant_retry.spec: T=1e5 DNS (Chandler-Kerswell's own shortest sourced length) + genuine hookstep + ~100 Newton attempts, SAME N=24 resolution as leg 353 (resolution not upgraded)
minimum_viable_spec_compliant_retry.legs: 2 (1 for hookstep implementation+validation, 1 for the long-DNS run + O(100)-attempt search, plausibly needing to run as a background multi-hour job across a session boundary the way leg 353's 2-leg ceiling was pre-sized for a harder-than-expected outcome)
minimum_viable_spec_compliant_retry.compute: ~4.9h DNS + ~17-28h Newton search =~ 22-33 hours (roughly 1-1.5 days) wall-clock, single CPU core, pure numpy, current solver as-is

full_literature_scale_retry.spec: T=5e6 DNS (Lucas & Kerswell's own scale) + genuine hookstep + full guess catalogue (thousands of guesses, hundreds of Newton attempts), matching resolution unclear (not costed -- flagged separately)
full_literature_scale_retry.legs: not a single-session leg budget at all on this leg's CPU-only pure-numpy solver -- DNS alone is ~10.2 days wall-clock; this is a MULTI-WEEK background compute commitment, or requires porting the solver to GPU (the literature's own workaround) before it becomes leg-budget-feasible
full_literature_scale_retry.compute: ~10.2 days DNS + proportionally more Newton search time; not further costed because the DNS term alone already dominates any plausible leg-session budget by 2 orders of magnitude

residual_risk_named: sample-size risk: even fully spec-compliant, the source papers' own 4-10% per-attempt RPO success rate means a modest retry (tens of attempts) can still come up empty by chance, indistinguishable from a genuine capability gap -- only ~50-100+ attempts make a null result informative

hookstep is not universally convergent even in the source's own hands: 1308.3356 reports the SAME Newton-GMRES-hookstep code failing to converge at the two endpoints of a continuation branch (Re=15.03 and Re=26.68) -- a correctly implemented hookstep is not a convergence guarantee, it is a substantially better-but-still-fallible globalization

resolution gap not costed: leg 353 ran at N=24; 1406.1820's own text implies their 'full' recurrence check used a much finer grid (Nx=Ny=128, i.e. max wavenumber 42 vs leg 353's much coarser truncation) -- this was never one of leg 353's two DECLARED simplifications, so it is out of scope for THIS retry spec, but it is a plausible third gap that a spec-compliant-on-two-axes retry could still trip over, and would need its own leg to price

GPU dependency: BOTH source papers needed either GPU acceleration (1406.1820) or CPU-months (1207.4682) to reach their DNS lengths -- the full-literature-scale retry is not affordable on this leg's current CPU-only pure-numpy solver stack within normal leg-session budgets; only the minimum-viable (T=1e5) version is

gate_reasoning: (a) sourced requirements table: 3 papers, each with directly-quoted DNS length, recurrence threshold, globalization method, and author-reported success rate. (b) costed retry spec: 2 legs / ~22-33 hours compute for a minimum-viable spec-compliant retry, multi-week/GPU-dependent for full literature scale, with four named residual risks (sample-size, hookstep non-universality, resolution gap, GPU dependency) -- sufficient for the user to rule on numbers without further literature work.
